html: The Shita Got'ine, "people of the mountains", are a Dene people of the Mackenzie Mountains in the Northwest Territories, Canada, also called the Mountain Dene. They hunted caribou, moose and Dall sheep in the high valleys and came down to the Mackenzie River to trade furs. They are known for moose-skin boats, built to carry families and meat downriver in spring. In the 1900s most settled at Tulita and other river communities, alongside other Sahtu Dene such as the K'áálǫ Got'ine. Their lands fall under the Sahtu Dene and Métis land claim, signed with Canada in 1993.
